checks.reason: Get-started page: API authentication uses Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Users without a role on the app can grant permissions only after each permission passes App Review and the app is published, so multi-tenant use needs Meta review.
Endpoints are plain HTTP GET/POST Graph-style resources (e.g. GET /refresh_access_token); no GraphQL or SOAP.
Meta's MCP hub lists only Meta Ads, Meta Social Technologies (devtools) and WhatsApp Business Tools servers, none for Threads; Threads MCPs found are third-party.
Buildable and testable with tester accounts today, but App Review gates launch to other users.

Creating an application under Settings > Advanced yields an Application ID/Secret for the OAuth2 flow (third-party doc; gumroad.com/api is client-rendered and returned no text); Gumroad's own MCP also uses OAuth.
Gumroad has no monthly fee (free to join, per-sale fee only) and any account can create an API application; no review or install cap found.
UNSETTLED: the official API page is client-rendered and returned no text to fetch, so REST could not be confirmed from an opened page; no evidence of another style.
Gumroad, Inc. documents its own remote MCP endpoint https://gumroad.com/claude/v1/mcp with OAuth access to the user's store.
Self-serve OAuth credentials at $0 and an official MCP; nothing blocks building and testing today.
API authenticates with an API token created in Console, sent as Bearer; the API docs do not mention OAuth (OAuth exists only for the MCP server).
Free plan at $0 with $5 monthly usage, no credit card, renews monthly (not a trial).
Docs: the API is organized around RESTful HTTP endpoints.
Apify hosts https://mcp.apify.com and publishes github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server.
Free self-serve token, REST API and an official MCP; no gate.
Public API requests authenticate with a Clay API key in the clay-api-key header; OAuth appears only for the MCP server.

API/CLI limits table includes a Free plan (100 results per 30 days) separate from Trial; pricing lists 'Build with Clay via CLI / API' on Free. Tables are Enterprise-only, which is a caveat rather than the access gate.
Public API is HTTP endpoints with request/response schemas; the CLI is secondary, so primary style is rest.
Clay runs the MCP server at https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp with OAuth+PKCE and open Dynamic Client Registration.
Buildable on Free, but tiny free result quotas, webhooks/HTTP API on Growth+ and Tables on Enterprise limit testing.
Query API supports Basic and Bearer auth; requests use a valid database user's login credentials, so basic (username/password) is the typical toolkit path.
AuraDB Free at $0, no credit card or payment method required; no app review for multi-tenant use since each user brings their own instance.
Query API is HTTP (POST /db/neo4j/query/v2); Bolt is driver-only, so for a toolkit the HTTP API is the primary style.
Repo in the neo4j GitHub org described as 'Neo4j official MCP Server', documented at neo4j.com/docs/mcp (local, username/password).
Free self-serve, but every tenant must supply its own instance URI and credentials (per-tenant setup caveat).
Docs: 'Any integrations that allow other users to grant access to Airtable should use OAuth.'
Free plan includes 1,000 API calls per workspace per month; the OAuth integration guide requires only privacy policy and terms URLs before sharing, with no review or install cap.
Docs: the API 'closely follows REST semantics.'
Airtable documents its own MCP server at https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp (OAuth or PAT), 'available to all users on all plans.'
Self-serve OAuth integration with no review step; free tier is enough to build and test (1,000 calls/month is a usage limit, not a gate).
Every request needs a dashboard-generated key (ipx_live_...) sent as Bearer in the Authorization header; OAuth is only listed as 'Coming Q3 2026' for QuickBooks/Stripe apps.

UNSETTLED: the developer page lists API tiers starting at a $99/mo Developer plan and the homepage says API access needs the Credit Pack or Unlimited plan, but the MCP server docs (ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server) describe free tools at 10 audits/day per API key, so vendor pages conflict on a free key path.
Reference page is titled 'REST API · v1' (base URL is a Supabase edge function).
Vendor developer page documents its own MCP endpoint https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp (author iPayX Protocol), also documented at ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server.
REST API and official MCP exist, but full API use sits behind paid tiers (free tier is 3 audits), so a paid gate limits testing.
